title: ECB Economic Bulletin Issue 6, 2026 — the comprehensive edition carrying the September staff projections' integrated discussion
source: EST: ecb.europa.eu Economic Bulletin index (press/economic-bulletin/html/index.en.html), fetched direct 2026-09-08 by the ecb-decision-2026-09-10 D-2 pulse-check adjacency sweep. The page states the schedule verbatim — the Bulletin is 'released eight times a year, two weeks after each monetary policy meeting' — and names the next release outright: 'Issue 6, 2026 - 24 September 2026'. The same page also states that the March/June/September/December editions are the comprehensive ones, carrying an 'integrated discussion of the staff macroeconomic projections on inflation, growth, public finances, and external trade'. Corroborated by the realized cadence on that index: Issue 5, 2026 published 6 August 2026, exactly two weeks after the 23 July 2026 monetary-policy meeting this calendar already tracks; 2026-09-24 is exactly two weeks after 2026-09-10. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep, and because this calendar carries no confirmed source prefix for a non-Fed central bank — the same taxonomy reason ecb-decision-2026-09-10 itself is filed estimate despite a direct ECB primary. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the ecb-decision-2026-09-10 D-2 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-08). This calendar tracks the ECB's decision, account, quiet periods, bank lending survey and monetary developments, but no Economic Bulletin edition. This one earns a row for a narrow, dated reason and nothing more: it is the ONLY scheduled venue between the 09-10 decision and the 10-08 account that publishes the staff's own written reasoning around the September projection round, and the parent ledger's single scoreable cell (2028 HICP against June's 2.0%, registered as FT-ecb-decision-2026-09-10-1) is a projection-round number whose surrounding argument lands here rather than at the presser. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the parent ledger's own finding: `symbols: []`, no house playbook is rates-keyed, and the parent's leg 8 argues explicitly that no tracked name (NVDA/AVGO/MRVL/CRWV) carries a euro-rates channel — a bulletin two weeks after a fully-priced decision is a reading document, not a price event. Sequencing note for whoever researches it: 09-24 sits AFTER fomc-2026-09-16, so it is also the first ECB text published into a post-FOMC rate backdrop, and BEFORE ecb-account-2026-10-08, which carries the Council's deliberations rather than the staff's write-up. Proposed as an estimate; it widens caution and licenses nothing.
